No discussions of the *Nandāpetivatthu* were identified in the corpus of secondary literature provided, but computational analysis by DharmaNexus documents extensive textual reuse within the Pali tradition, recording 228 matching passages across 26 canonical and commentarial texts [DharmaNexus]. In addition to its commentary, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (which matches 99 segments, especially §3.3–18.4) and the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the text shares significant verse clusters with neighboring accounts in the *Petavatthu*, such as *Mattāpetivatthu* (Pv 15, §10.4–19.1), *Sāriputtattheramātupetivatthu* (Pv 14, §10.4–15.4), *Saṁsāramocakapetivatthu* (Pv 13), and *Seriṇīpetivatthu* (Pv 31) [DharmaNexus]. It also shares recurrent formulaic verses (particularly §13.1–15.4) with numerous poems in the *Vimānavatthu*, including *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Dīpavimānavatthu* (Vv 9), and *Tiladakkhiṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 10) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with Tibetan translations (D0353 and D4106) and the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99), though these represent machine text alignments rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
